title: [telemetry] exports metrics and logs but no spans, while reporting traces=true
description:
Found 2026-11-22 while turning on OpenTelemetry for the interop host.
mimid starts, logs "OpenTelemetry export configured ... traces=true",
and exports metrics and logs but NOT ONE span.

MEASURED, with a collector on loopback writing every signal to a file:

  batches:     {'resourceMetrics': 10, 'resourceLogs': 7, 'resourceSpans': 1}
  log records: 44
  spans:       [('handmade', 1)]

'handmade' is a span I POSTed to the collector by hand as a control, so
the only span in the file is the one mimid did not send. Metrics and
logs arrive continuously; spans never do.

RULED OUT, in this order:
- The collector. A hand-made POST to http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces
  returns 200 and lands in the file, so the receiver, the traces
  pipeline and the file exporter all work.
- The endpoint and transport. telemetry.rs builds all three exporters
  with .with_http() and the standard paths (/v1/traces, /v1/logs,
  /v1/metrics) against the same base URL. Metrics and logs on that base
  URL work, so the base URL and HTTP transport are right.
- The log filter level. Spans are at default INFO
  (#[tracing::instrument(name = "protocol_request", ...)] in http.rs with
  no `level =` anywhere in the file), and RUST_LOG is unset so the
  filter is "info". Setting RUST_LOG=info,mimid_server=trace changed
  nothing: still no spans.
- A missing flush. Restarting mimid runs Telemetry::shutdown, which
  calls tracer.shutdown(), and no spans appeared across several
  restarts.

WHERE THAT POINTS. Metrics go through a separate path (the global meter
and the Metrics struct), while traces and logs BOTH come from
Telemetry::layers() into the tracing subscriber. Logs work, so the layer
stack is installed and reaching the subscriber. So the fault is specific
to the traces half: tracing_opentelemetry::layer().with_tracer(
provider.tracer("mimid")), composed by Layer::and_then(traces, logs) in
telemetry.rs layers().

Not chased further here, because logs plus metrics already give the
interop day what it needs and this is a code investigation rather than a
deployment step. Worth looking at whether the Option<OpenTelemetryLayer>
in that and_then is being applied, and whether the SdkTracerProvider
needs to be installed globally for the layer's tracer to record.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: spans are the signal that makes a failed
interop exchange legible -- which endpoint, which peer, how long, and
the `peer` field each protocol_request span records. Logs give the
events but not the correlation. Also, the startup line says traces=true
when nothing is exported, so an operator has no way to notice.

LIVE STATE, and it is useful as it stands: a collector runs on dokr
(docker container otelcol-mimid, OTLP on 127.0.0.1:4318 only, no UI, no
outbound network) writing every signal to
/var/log/otelcol-mimid/mimid-telemetry.jsonl, rotating at 64 MB with 5
backups. mimid's [telemetry] points at it. So the interop day will leave
a greppable record of metrics and log events; only spans are missing.

Two deployment notes for anyone redoing this:
- The collector image runs as uid 10001. The output directory must be
  owned by it; root-owned 755 fails with "can't open new logfile ...
  permission denied" and the collector drops every batch while looking
  healthy.
- Those errors appear only in `docker logs otelcol-mimid`, not in
  mimid's journal, because mimid's exporter considers a buffered send
  successful.
